_comment: Clock-domain letters and block letters for the net-naming stage tag.
Read by tools/lint-rtl.py; nothing is generated from it, because only the
domain   letter for the clock domain the signal is generated in
block    letter for the block that generates it
NN       two-digit pipe stage within that block
l|h      generating clock edge: h = posedge, l = negedge
CLOSED at the block-level grill-me (2026-09-23). 14 block types, 45
instances. Letters I, O and 0 are avoided for tag readability.
Open item A-2 is CLOSED by this list: 14 of 24 usable letters are taken
and 8 remain spare, so the single-letter tag format holds and does not
need widening. Two of the spare letters are taken below for things that
A-2's sub-question -- do testbench-side memory interfaces consume block
letters -- answers itself from the partition: EXB is the coherent
boundary and everything past it is testbench, so nothing beyond EXB is
tagged and no letter is spent on it.

domains.doc: The core clock domain, and the only functional one. Each block receives it twice: `clk`, gated for the block, and `clk_free`, ungated for the wake detector. Both are the same frequency, so this remains a single domain and §6's revisit trigger (multiple FREQUENCY domains) has not fired.

DFT clock. Asynchronous to core by construction, which is why its domain segment is not `core`. Nothing uses it yet; registered so the first signal crossing from it is a lint finding rather than a surprise.

blocks.name: fet
blocks.doc: Fetch, L1 I-cache, ITLB, length decode and align.

blocks.name: dec
blocks.doc: Format decode, 6-wide output, and two separate illegal-instruction obligations: reserved fields must be zero, and a legal field must not hold an unallocated value (srd selectors 2-15). The second is a range comparison, not a zero comparison, so allocating a selector later is a one-line change to a named check.

blocks.name: ooe
blocks.doc: RAT, free list, RS, 4 ROBs, scheduler, wakeup/select, squash, demotion trigger. Most-connected block, and first in the risk-first build order.

blocks.name: rcu
blocks.doc: Physical register file (flop array), predicate file, predicate ALU, collective crossbar.

blocks.name: lane
blocks.doc: 32-bit lane with 16/8/4-bit sections, SFU, cvt. The only multi-instance block; anything crossing lanes is tested in RCU, which holds the crossbar.

blocks.name: miu
blocks.doc: 4 AGU pipes, load and store buffers, disambiguation, TLB, page-table walker, exclusive ownership.

blocks.name: spm
blocks.doc: 128 KB scratchpad, 32 banks x 32 bits, conflict resolver.

blocks.name: dcu
blocks.doc: L1 data cache, 4 lookups per cycle, probe/invalidate port. NOTE the letter is `c`, not `d` -- `d` is DEC.

blocks.name: mlc
blocks.doc: Shared cache, merges I and D traffic, coherent boundary.

blocks.name: rau
blocks.doc: Warp slots, PRF partitions, SPM regions, CTA launch, warp-to-CTA-to-grid tables, kill masks, migration FSM, forward-progress guard. Moved early in the build order because so many blocks depend on its interfaces.

blocks.name: syu
blocks.doc: Barrier table, 64 entries, epoch-tagged, CTA-scoped. A §7 formal target.

blocks.name: pca
blocks.doc: Parked context array, banked 1r1w, 28 parked warps. Dumb storage plus a migration bus; policy is RAU's.

blocks.name: cru
blocks.doc: Control and status registers, sticky fault record, performance counters.

blocks.name: exb
blocks.doc: Protocol bridge to TileLink TL-C. The one boundary that does not follow the interface conventions, which is what keeps the exception to a single port.

blocks.name: reset
blocks.doc: RESERVED, not a design block: the reset distribution network, which does not share a numbering space with any block's datapath. A synchronous reset cannot be delivered globally in one cycle; it is pipelined, and how deep it is on arrival depends on physical distance. `z` rather than `r` because the grill-me assigned `r` to RCU -- an earlier draft of this registry had the collision. Reset nets are exempt from stage arithmetic.

blocks.name: reference
blocks.doc: PROVISIONAL, not a design block: pre-Stage-2 reference material and lint fixtures, so the naming rules have something to check. Was `x` until the grill-me assigned `x` to CRU.
